description: The supplied image is not a scientific figure: it is a publisher's "Check for updates" badge (Crossref-style update-alert logo) rendered as a small square graphic on a white background. Centred in the upper part of the graphic is a red ribbon/bookmark shape with a notched (swallow-tail) lower edge, enclosed by an open ring made of two coloured arc segments — a light-blue arc on the right and upper right and a yellow arc on the left and lower left — with a small gap at the top left of the ring where the two colours meet. Below the emblem, in dark grey sans-serif type, the words "Check for updates" appear on two centred lines, "Check for" above "updates". There are no axes, no units, no scale bar, no legend, no data points, no sample labels and no annotations of any other kind; the image contains no material, alloy, phase, composition, processing condition or measured quantity. It therefore carries no microstructural, crystallographic, spectroscopic or property information about FeMnAlC steels and cannot support any claim about the composition-microstructure correlation discussed in the paper. It is an editorial metadata graphic, not a data panel; the paper title and abstract given in the context are not represented anywhere in the pixels.

subfigures.description: A publisher 'Check for updates' badge: a red bookmark/ribbon emblem ringed by a segmented blue-and-yellow circular arrow, with the two-line text 'Check for updates' printed beneath it in dark grey. No axes, data, scale bar or scientific labelling are present.

observations.observation: The image is a publisher 'Check for updates' badge, not a scientific data figure; the only text is 'Check for updates' printed in two centred lines below the emblem.
The emblem consists of a red bookmark/ribbon shape with a notched bottom edge, surrounded by an open ring formed from a light-blue arc and a yellow arc.
No axes, axis labels, units, scale bar, legend, colour scale or numeric values appear anywhere in the image.
No sample, alloy, phase, composition or processing-condition label (e.g. any FeMnAlC designation) is visible in the image.
The figure contains no microstructural, diffraction, spectroscopic or property data and therefore provides no evidence about the composition-microstructure correlation of low-density FeMnAlC steels.
